title: Learning Cole-Hopf Coordinates for Stochastic Growth Dynamics: the KPZ class
authors: Lorenzo Mensi, Simone Cuonzo, Maria Chiara Angelini, Sergio Chibbaro, Cyril Furtlehner, Alberto Rosso
abstract: Inferring effective equations from observations of nonlinear stochastic processes is challenging because individual trajectories are noisy realizations, while the relevant physical information is encoded in ensemble statistics. We introduce a data-driven framework that learns a change of variables in which nonlinear stochastic dynamics become linear. The model combines a neural change of representation with a linear stochastic latent evolution and is trained through a short-time moment-matching objective, thereby avoiding trajectory \rev{simulation} during optimization. This construction yields an interpretable generative model: both the learned transformation and the latent evolution operators can be directly inspected.   We validate the method on the one-dimensional Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) equation, a paradigmatic model of stochastic growth for which the Cole--Hopf transformation maps the nonlinear dynamics to the stochastic heat equation. From simulated height trajectories alone, the model recovers the local exponential Cole--Hopf map and the associated linear stochastic operator. Generated trajectories reproduce the main statistical signatures of the KPZ universality class, including the growth law $\mathrm{Var}(h^{t})\sim t^{2β}$ with $β=1/3$ and the GOE Tracy--Widom height distribution for flat initial conditions. These results show that interpretable stochastic equations can be inferred from data by learning representations in which the dynamics closes in a simple form. Furthermore the development of the physical informed learning permits to get insights on the physics of the dynamical process.
summary: This work presents a novel, data-driven method to infer the underlying mathematical structure of complex nonlinear stochastic processes, using the KPZ equation as a prime example. By learning a change of variables that linearizes the dynamics, the authors recover the exact Cole-Hopf map and the associated linear stochastic operator directly from height profiles. This provides a powerful, interpretable tool for extracting fundamental physical laws from noisy observational data.
main_problem: The central challenge is inferring the underlying effective stochastic differential equation governing a nonlinear process when only noisy, ensemble-averaged trajectory data is available.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated a data-driven framework that recovers the exact Cole-Hopf transformation and the associated linear stochastic operator for the KPZ equation, reproducing universal statistical signatures.
method: They propose a framework combining a neural change of representation with a linear latent stochastic evolution, trained using a short-time moment-matching objective to ensure interpretability.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the one-dimensional Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) equation, a canonical model for stochastic interface growth, which is known to linearize via the Cole-Hopf transformation.
key_observables: Growth law $	ext{Var}(h_t) \sim t^{2 eta}$ with $ eta=1/3$, and the GOE Tracy-Widom height distribution.
important_parameters:
The coupling constants ($\lambda, 
u$) and noise strength ($D$) of the KPZ equation are implicitly recovered.
main_assumptions: The interpretable model assumes the latent dynamics are linear and that the change of variables is local in space; the training relies on matching short-time moment statistics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate numerical KPZ trajectories showing characteristic roughening, and comparisons are made for spatial correlation functions ($G_t(\xi)$) to validate the recovered dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of inferring SDEs from data, details the interpretable latent-SDE framework using moment matching, validates it on the KPZ equation by recovering the known Cole-Hopf map, and compares this to a more general, non-interpretable autoencoder approach.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the methodology—learning an underlying, simple, and interpretable governing equation from complex data—is highly relevant for modeling open quantum systems or non-equilibrium dynamics where the full Hamiltonian is unknown.
